summary:
I've been chasing down a media stack problem that looked like flakiness but wasn't. Sonarr kept losing episodes to "Unable to Import Automatically," and I assumed bad downloads until I checked the actual mismatch: releases were arriving under Japanese titles while my library used English ones, and the scene-mapping service that bridges them had been silently dead for over a week. Once I saw that, the fix was a manual-import API call with hardlink-preserving copy mode instead of a move — so seeding continued and nothing got duplicated on disk.

The other half of that stack was a queue that looked stalled — 75 downloads sitting at 0% for ten hours. Turned out to be five zero-seeder torrents hogging every download slot while good torrents waited behind them. I also learned the hard way that blocklisting a dead release doesn't stop it from being re-grabbed, since the blocklist is keyed to release name plus indexer — a different indexer just serves it right back. A seeder floor turned out to be the actual guard, not the blocklist.

On the automation side, I run a local LLM as an agent brain, and I recently swapped in an uncensored variant after the stock one started refusing ordinary lookups. That surfaced a nasty, silent failure mode: setting its "reasoning budget" to zero didn't disable reasoning, it broke tool-calling outright — the model would type out a fake tool call as plain text instead of actually invoking one, and just sit there waiting for a response that would never come. Looked exactly like the model being slow or broken; it was neither. I ran an A/B against a second candidate model to see if it handled tool selection better, and the benchmark said no difference — which was itself informative, since it told me my test harness was too easy to catch the real failure mode I cared about, not that the models were actually equivalent.

Mostly this stretch has been less "build the feature" and more "figure out why the thing that looks broken is actually a different thing entirely."

highlights.oneLiner: chasing a reasoning-budget=0 bug that silently broke tool-calling
A/B'd a second model against the brain; benchmark was too easy to tell
